case_title: Mahadevappa v. State of Karnataka rep. by Public Prosecutor
accused_occupation: Constable in the police (Police Station, Kaladagi)
weapon: Kerosene oil (poured on the victim and set alight)
evidence_type: Dying declaration to father at hospital; ocular testimony of parents and relatives on prior cruelty and demands; medical evidence (post-mortem, doctor PW-6); FSL report; recovery of kerosene bottle; circumstantial evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Habitual drinking; repeated demands for money from the victim and her parents; ill-treatment and assault of the victim beginning soon after marriage; death within seven years of marriage (17 months); victim's death by burning
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of all charges (s.498A and s.302 IPC); dowry demand and homicidal death not proved
high_court_outcome: State's appeal allowed; acquittal reversed; convicted under ss.498A and 302 IPC; life imprisonment imposed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.498A (cruelty/dowry harassment) and IPC s.302 (murder)
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim had been married about seventeen months earlier. The prosecution said the accused drank alcohol heavily, repeatedly demanded money from the victim and her parents, and at times beat and ill-treated the victim. Several witnesses, including the victim's parents, a brother-in-law and a relative, described these incidents, and said the victim had complained of them in letters and in person. On the morning of the incident, around 8 a.m., the victim was found with severe burns in the house. Only the accused and the victim were present. She was taken to a government hospital, where she told her father that the accused had poured kerosene on her and set her on fire. She died the same evening. The victim's father lodged a complaint and police investigated. The investigation collected a post-mortem report and a forensic report and seized a bottle of kerosene from the room. Kerosene was found on the victim's body and a bottle of kerosene lay in the room. Broken bangles were found in the room. The burn injuries were mainly on the upper body, and the blouse was burnt. The accused's explanation was that the victim's sari caught fire accidentally while she was boiling water on an oven. The doctor and investigating officer gave evidence. Some witnesses were cross-examined at length by the defence.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from severe burn injuries sustained on 02.10.1995, about 17 months after marriage
motive: alleged: Dowry-related demands for money from the victim and her parents, which she could not meet, and strained relations; the court did not expressly decide the motive for the killing
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence of father (PW-1), mother (PW-4), brother-in-law (PW-5) and relative (PW-17) on cruelty and demands; victim's statement to father at hospital; doctor (PW-6) evidence; post-mortem and FSL reports; kerosene on body and bottle in room; broken bangles; burns mainly on upper body and burnt blouse
witness_credibility: Four witnesses found consistent with no contradiction on material issues despite lengthy cross-examination; parents held to be most natural and material witnesses; no reason shown for them to lie
trial_duration: offence: 02.10.1995; trial judgment: 31.05.2000; High Court: 03.01.2007; Supreme Court: 07.01.2019
legal_representation: Accused: Mallikarjun S. Mylar, Manjunath, Ms. Umme Salma, Ms. E. R. Sumathy (Advocates). State: Joseph Aristotle S., Mrs. Priya Aristotle, Shiva P., Ms. Aruna Hannah Dutta, Ms. Anitha Shenoy (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed with post-mortem and FSL report; charge-sheet filed; committed to Sessions Court
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted of all charges. High Court: State's appeal allowed; convicted under ss.498A and 302 IPC; life imprisonment. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed; conviction upheld
prosecution_argument: Trial court failed to properly appreciate the evidence; High Court rightly held both demand of dowry and murder proved beyond reasonable doubt
defence_argument: No case made for reversing the acquittal; no dowry demand or murder proved; hostile witnesses should lead to discarding the prosecution case; accidental death suggested
legal_principle_applied: Parents' testimony on cruelty and demands treated as natural and reliable; cruelty assessed under s.498A Explanations (a) and (b); homicidal versus accidental death decided on circumstantial evidence proved beyond reasonable doubt; hostile witnesses not fatal
